blocks.prompt: 9 We say that two vectors \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) in space are parallel if there is a scalar \(c\) such that \(\underline{v} = c\underline{w}\). The vectors point in the same direction if \(c > 0\) and in the opposite direction if \(c < 0\). (a) Find two vectors of length 2 parallel to the vector \(\underline{v} = 2\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Two answers are expected: one along \(\underline{v}\) and one opposite to it.
Plan: make the unit vector \(\underline{v}/|\underline{v}|\), then multiply by \(2\) and by \(-2\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{v} = 2\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\), required length 2.
To find: two vectors of length 2 parallel to \(\underline{v}\).
Method: \(\pm 2\,\dfrac{\underline{v}}{|\underline{v}|}\): the unit vector fixes the direction, \(\pm 2\) fixes the length and the sense.

Unit vector
\[\dfrac{\underline{v}}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\underline{i} - \dfrac{2}{3}\underline{j} + \dfrac{2}{3}\underline{k}\]
Why: Dividing by the length gives length 1.

Multiply by \(2\) and by \(-2\)
\[\tfrac{2}{3}\underline{i} - \tfrac{4}{3}\underline{j} + \tfrac{4}{3}\underline{k}\]
\[-\tfrac{2}{3}\underline{i} + \tfrac{4}{3}\underline{j} - \tfrac{4}{3}\underline{k}\]
Why: \(c = 2/6 = 1/3 > 0\) gives the same direction; \(c = -1/3 < 0\) gives the opposite direction.

Check
\[\dfrac{4 + 16 + 16}{9} = \dfrac{36}{9} = 4\]
\[\sqrt{4} = 2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both vectors have the same component sizes, so both have length 2.

blocks.prompt: 9 We say that two vectors \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) in space are parallel if there is a scalar \(c\) such that \(\underline{v} = c\underline{w}\). The vectors point in the same direction if \(c > 0\) and in the opposite direction if \(c < 0\). (b) Find the constant \(a\) so that the vectors \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{w} = a\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} - 12\underline{k}\) are parallel.
blocks.explanation:
Parallel means \(\underline{w} = c\underline{v}\) for one number \(c\).
The \(\underline{j}\) and \(\underline{k}\) parts are fully known, so they give \(c\); the \(\underline{i}\) part then gives \(a\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = a\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} - 12\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} \parallel \underline{v}\).
To find: \(a\).
Method: \(\underline{w} = c\underline{v}\); compare components.

Write \(\underline{w} = c\underline{v}\)
\[a\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} - 12\underline{k}\]
\[= c\underline{i} - 3c\underline{j} + 4c\underline{k}\]
Why: Definition of parallel vectors.

Find \(c\) from \(\underline{j}\) and \(\underline{k}\)
\[9 = -3c \Rightarrow c = -3\]
\[-12 = 4c \Rightarrow c = -3\]
Why: Both give the same \(c\), so the vectors can indeed be parallel.

Find \(a\)
\[a = c \times 1 = -3\]
Why: Compare the \(\underline{i}\) components.

blocks.prompt: 9 We say that two vectors \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) in space are parallel if there is a scalar \(c\) such that \(\underline{v} = c\underline{w}\). The vectors point in the same direction if \(c > 0\) and in the opposite direction if \(c < 0\). (c) Find a vector of length 5 in the direction opposite that of \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Opposite direction means a negative multiple of \(\underline{v}\).
Plan: unit vector \(\underline{v}/|\underline{v}|\), then multiply by \(-5\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), length 5, opposite direction.
To find: the required vector.
Method: \(-5\,\dfrac{\underline{v}}{|\underline{v}|}\).

Multiply the unit vector by \(-5\)
\[-\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{14}}(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k})\]
\[= \dfrac{-5\underline{i} + 10\underline{j} - 15\underline{k}}{\sqrt{14}}\]
Why: The minus sign reverses the direction; 5 sets the length.

Check
\[\dfrac{25 + 100 + 225}{14} = \dfrac{350}{14} = 25\]
\[\sqrt{25} = 5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Length 5, and \(c = -5/\sqrt{14} < 0\), so the direction is opposite.

blocks.prompt: 9 We say that two vectors \(\underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\) in space are parallel if there is a scalar \(c\) such that \(\underline{v} = c\underline{w}\). The vectors point in the same direction if \(c > 0\) and in the opposite direction if \(c < 0\). (d) Find \(a\) and \(b\) so that the vectors \(3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\) and \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) are parallel.
blocks.explanation:
Parallel: \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} - 2\underline{k} = c(3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 4\underline{k})\).
The \(\underline{k}\) part is fully known, so it gives \(c\); then the \(\underline{i}\) and \(\underline{j}\) parts give \(a\) and \(b\).
steps:
Given: \(3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\) and \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) are parallel.
To find: \(a\) and \(b\).
Method: write the second as \(c\) times the first and compare components.

Write the condition
\[a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\]
\[= 3c\underline{i} - c\underline{j} + 4c\underline{k}\]
Why: Definition of parallel vectors.

Find \(c\) from \(\underline{k}\)
\[-2 = 4c \Rightarrow c = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: Only the \(\underline{k}\) components are both known numbers.

Find \(a\) and \(b\)
\[a = 3c = -\dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[b = -c = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: Compare the \(\underline{i}\) and \(\underline{j}\) components.

Check
\[-\tfrac{1}{2}(3\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 4\underline{k})\]
\[= -\tfrac{3}{2}\underline{i} + \tfrac{1}{2}\underline{j} - 2\underline{k} \;\checkmark\]
Why: This is exactly \(a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) with our values.
